stem.en: On a sunny afternoon the sand on a beach is much hotter than the sea beside it. Why?

text.en: Sunlight falls only on the sand, not on the sea.
Heat stays near the surface of sand, but mixes deep into water.

feedback.en: Yes. Water shares the same heat through much more depth.

text.en: The sand is closer to the Sun than the water.

feedback.en: They are at almost the same distance from the Sun.

explanation.en: Sunlight warms only a thin top layer of sand, so that layer gets hot quickly. In the sea, heat is mixed down through deep water, so the surface warms slowly.

hints.en: Sunlight reaches both. What happens to the heat after that?
